title: Eating out with friends
goal: Order street food and restaurant meals for a group, say a dish is too spicy or needs salt, say what you feel like eating, and sort out the bill: a treat, halves or your share.
intro:
Eating out in India is a group sport: dishes are ordered for the table, everyone has an opinion about the spice, and the end of the meal brings the famous fight over who pays. In this unit you'll order **एक प्लेट गोलगप्पे** at a street stall and **दो बिरयानी** at a restaurant, complain politely (**नमक थोड़ा कम है** 'it needs a bit of salt'), and handle the bill (**आज की ट्रीट मेरी तरफ़ से!** 'today's on me!').

The grammar is about amounts — **too, enough, a little** (बहुत ज़्यादा, काफ़ी, थोड़ा, कम) — and the everyday way to say **'I feel like…'**: **मेरा पिज़्ज़ा खाने का मन है**.

grammar.title: Too, enough, a little
grammar.body:
**Too / way too**: Hindi has no separate word for 'too'. It uses **ज़्यादा** 'more, too much', and **बहुत ज़्यादा** for 'far too': **बहुत ज़्यादा तीखा** 'way too spicy'. A softer complaint is **कुछ ज़्यादा ही**: कुछ ज़्यादा ही मीठा है 'it's a touch too sweet'.

**Not enough** is usually said with **कम** 'less': **नमक कम है** 'there isn't enough salt', **मिर्च कम है** 'it's not spicy enough'. To ask for a change: **थोड़ा कम** तीखा 'a bit less spicy', **थोड़ा और** 'a bit more'.

**Enough**: **काफ़ी** after the thing: **इतना काफ़ी है** 'this is enough', **पैसे काफ़ी नहीं हैं** 'the money isn't enough'. On its own, **बस!** means 'that's enough, stop'.

**A little / some**: **थोड़ा**, which agrees: थोड़ा पानी, **थोड़ी** चाय, **थोड़े** समोसे.

**So … that**: **इतना … कि**: इतना तीखा था **कि** … 'it was so spicy that…'. इतना agrees too: इतनी तीखी बिरयानी.

The trap: **काफ़ी** *before* an adjective means 'quite, pretty': **काफ़ी अच्छा** 'pretty good', not 'good enough'. And ज़्यादा alone can mean 'more' or 'too much'; बहुत ज़्यादा makes 'too much' clear.

grammar.title: I feel like…: मेरा … का मन है
grammar.body:
To say what you feel like doing, Hindi says your **मन** 'mind, heart' has a wish:

**मेरा** + verb-**ने का मन है** — मेरा पिज़्ज़ा **खाने का मन है** 'I feel like (eating) pizza'.

The pieces: **मेरा** (whose मन), the activity as an oblique infinitive + **का** (खाने का, जाने का, पीने का), then **मन है**. Because मन is masculine, it is always **का**, never की.

**Right now**: **मन कर रहा है**: आज बाहर खाने का मन कर रहा है 'I really feel like eating out today'. **दिल कर रहा है** means the same with more feeling.
**Just a thing**: noun + **का मन**: चाय का मन है? 'fancy some tea?'
**Asking the group**: **किसका** … का मन है? — **मेरा!** 'who's up for…? — me!'
**Not in the mood**: **मेरा मन नहीं है** — a soft, perfectly accepted way to say no.

The trap: the owner is **मेरा / तुम्हारा / उसका / हमारा**, not मुझे. Compare मुझे पिज़्ज़ा पसंद है 'I like pizza' (always) with मेरा पिज़्ज़ा खाने का मन है 'I feel like pizza' (now). **मूड** (unit 21) works the same way: खाना बनाने का मूड नहीं है.

culture: Indian friends rarely order one dish each: food is ordered **for the table** and shared, so **क्या मँगवाएँ?** 'what shall we order?' is a group discussion. Waiters and street vendors are called **भैया** (or a polite *excuse me*), and asking for **कम तीखा** 'less spicy' is completely normal; nobody will think less of you. Many groups have vegetarians, so dishes are discussed as **वेज** or **नॉन-वेज**. Paying is where the drama is: friends and relatives often fight to pay (**नहीं, नहीं, मैं दूँगा!**), and whoever has good news — a birthday, a new job, a promotion — is expected to give a **ट्रीट** ('**पार्टी दो!**'). Among students and young colleagues, splitting is normal, usually by UPI (**मैं तुम्हें भेज देता हूँ** 'I'll send it to you'). Tipping around 10% is appreciated in sit-down restaurants but not expected at street stalls or dhabas, and asking to pack up leftovers is never embarrassing.

tip.title: Street-food Hindi
tip.body:
- Order by the plate: **एक प्लेट** गोलगप्पे, **दो प्लेट** मोमोज़ — प्लेट stays the same after a number.
- Many snacks are plural nouns, so adjectives take **-े**: मोमोज़ अच्छे **हैं**, समोसे कुरकुरे **हैं**.
- Call the vendor **भैया**.
- Loved it? **मज़ा आ गया!**

tip.title: Ordering for a group
tip.body:
- Ask the group: **क्या मँगवाएँ?** 'what shall we order?'
- Order with **मेरे लिए** 'for me', **हमारे लिए** 'for us'.
- To the waiter: **भैया, … ले आना** (polite: **ले आइए**).
- English works with करना: ऑर्डर **कर दिया** 'I've ordered'.

tip.title: Too much, not enough, enough
tip.body:
- **बहुत ज़्यादा** = way too: बहुत ज़्यादा तीखा.
- Not enough = **कम**: नमक **कम** है 'it needs salt'. Ask for **थोड़ा कम** तीखा or **थोड़ा और**.
- Enough = **काफ़ी** after the thing: इतना **काफ़ी** है. **बस!** = 'that's enough'.
- Trap: काफ़ी **before** an adjective = 'quite': काफ़ी अच्छा 'pretty good'.
tip.pattern: बहुत ज़्यादा + adj  ·  noun + कम है  ·  इतना काफ़ी है

lessons.title: What do you feel like?

tip.title: मेरा … का मन है — I feel like…
tip.body:
- 'I feel like…' = **मेरा** + verb-**ने का मन है**: मेरा पिज़्ज़ा खाने का मन है.
- Right now, strongly: **मन कर रहा है**.
- The owner is **मेरा / तुम्हारा / उसका**, not मुझे. Always **का** (मन is masculine).
- **मेरा मन नहीं है** 'I don't feel like it' is a polite excuse.

lessons.title: Paying: a treat or halves?

tip.title: Sorting out the bill
tip.body:
- Ask for it: **भैया, बिल ले आना**.
- Treating: **आज की ट्रीट मेरी तरफ़ से!** Expect a friendly fight over who pays.
- Splitting: **आधा-आधा कर लेते हैं** or **बिल बाँट लेते हैं**; everyone pays **अपना हिस्सा**.
- Leftovers: **पैक कर दीजिए** is completely normal.

new: आज की ट्रीट मेरी तरफ़ से!

sentences.native: भैया, बिल ले आना और यह पैक कर देना।
sentences.roman: bhaiyā, bil le ānā aur yah paik kar denā.
sentences.en: Could you bring the bill, and pack this up?

sentences.native: बिल मैं दूँगा, तुम रहने दो।
sentences.roman: bil maiṃ dūṃgā, tum rahne do.
sentences.en: I'll get the bill, leave it.

sentences.native: प्रिया ने नई नौकरी की ट्रीट दी।
sentences.roman: Priyā ne naī naukrī kī ṭrīṭ dī.
sentences.en: Priya treated us for her new job.

sentences.native: चलो, बिल चार हिस्सों में बाँट लेते हैं।
sentences.roman: chalo, bil chār hissoṃ meṃ bāṃṭ lete haiṃ.
sentences.en: Let's split the bill four ways.

sentences.native: मेरा हिस्सा कितना हुआ?
sentences.roman: merā hissā kitnā huā?
sentences.en: How much is my share?

sentences.native: आधा-आधा कर लेते हैं, मैं तुम्हें यूपीआई कर दूँगी।
sentences.roman: ādhā-ādhā kar lete haiṃ, maiṃ tumheṃ yūpīāī kar dūṃgī.
sentences.en: Let's go halves, I'll UPI you. (woman speaking)

sentences.native: वेटर को थोड़ी टिप दे दो, वो बहुत अच्छा था।
sentences.roman: veṭar ko thoṛī ṭip de do, vo bahut achchhā thā.
sentences.en: Give the waiter a small tip, he was really good.

sentences.native: बचा हुआ खाना पैक कर दीजिए, घर ले जाएँगे।
sentences.roman: bachā huā khānā paik kar dījiye, ghar le jāyeṃge.
sentences.en: Please pack the leftovers, we'll take them home.

sentences.native: अरे, तुमने पिछली बार भी बिल दिया था!
sentences.roman: are, tumne pichhlī bār bhī bil diyā thā!
sentences.en: Hey, you paid last time too!
